parts.text: A student determines the resistance of a resistor. She uses the apparatus shown in Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 2.1, draw a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference (p.d.) across the resistor. [1]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text: correct voltmeter symbol in parallel with resistor

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student connects the crocodile clip to the resistance wire at the 100.0 cm mark on the metre ruler and measures the potential difference V 0 across the resistor. The voltmeter is shown in Fig. 2.2. Read and record the value of V 0 shown on the voltmeter in Fig. 2.2. V 0 = .......................................................V [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student moves the crocodile clip to a length of resistance wire l = 20.0 cm. Read and record in Table 2.1, the current for l = 20.0 cm, shown on the ammeter in Fig. 2.3. [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The student measures the current I for lengths of resistance wire l = 30.0 cm, l = 40.0 cm, l = 50.0 cm and l = 60.0 cm. Her readings are shown in Table 2.1. Table 2.1 l / cm I / A 20.0 30.0 0.22 40.0 0.30 50.0 0.39 60.0 0.42 Plot a graph of l / cm (y-axis) against I / A (x-axis). Draw a best-fit straight line. You do not need to start the axes at the origin (0,0). [4]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
graph:
•
axes labelled with quantity and unit
•
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
•
plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots
•
well-judged line and thin line

parts.label: i
parts.text: (e) (i) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(e)(i)
ms.text:
G present
and triangle method seen on graph

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the resistance R of the resistor. Use your value of V 0 from (b) and the equation: R = G × V 0 100k where k = 1.0 A R = ...................................................... Ω [1]

ms.label: 2(f)
ms.text:
valid practical source of inaccuracy, e.g:
uncertain connection point on crocodile clip /
resistance wire irregular / curved / not uniform / differing thickness along wire

ms.label: 2(g)
ms.text:
suitable improvement e.g:
reduce e.m.f. of power supply /
thinner resistance wire /
use of additional series / protective resistor to reduce current
